entities.summary:
Catigern (b. 405 CE) was a Roman economist or social scientist of the Late Antique period, active in the Roman Empire. He is known for his work on the economic systems of various empires, including the Roman Empire, the Persian Empire, and the Hellenistic kingdoms.

As a prominent figure in the intellectual circles of the time, Catigern contributed to the development of the Roman economic thought, which had a lasting impact on the Western world. His work built upon the foundations laid by earlier thinkers such as Aristotle and Xenophon, and influenced the economic thought of later scholars like John of Salisbury.

Despite his significant contributions, Catigern's work has been largely overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, such as the philosopher Boethius and the historian Procopius. Nevertheless, his ideas continue to be studied by historians and economists today, offering valuable insights into the economic systems of the ancient world.

One of the most striking aspects of Catigern's legacy is the enduring influence of his work on the development of modern economic thought. His emphasis on the importance of trade, commerce, and the state in the economy has shaped the course of economic history, from the rise of the medieval merchant class to the modern concept of the nation-state.

In conclusion, Catigern's work represents a significant milestone in the history of economic thought, and his contributions to the development of Roman economic thought continue to be felt today.
